name: Aradale Lunatic Asylum

facts.claim: Aradale was a psychiatric hospital in Ararat, begun in 1865 and opened to patients in 1867, closed as an asylum in 1993.
At its height it held up to 1000 patients, and the complex has up to 70 historic buildings.
Guided tours run from the Grano Street entrance, led by Friends of J Ward volunteers.

access_note: Tours on Sundays and Wednesdays at 10am; cancelled on Total Fire Ban days.

facts.claim: J Ward was Ararat County Gaol and later a psychiatric facility for the criminally insane; built 1859-1861.
Volunteer-led guided tours run daily and take 1 to 1.5 hours, and include a museum.
Tours visit the gaol cells, chapel and unmarked graves, with stories of former inmates.

name: Gum San Chinese Heritage Centre

facts.claim: Gum San means Gold Mountain; the centre stands on the site that started Ararat's gold rush.
Life-size scenes tell the story of 19th-century Chinese miners' sea voyage and trek to the Victorian goldfields.
It is managed by volunteers (Friends of Gum San) at 31 Lambert Street, Ararat.

name: Ararat Gallery TAMA

facts.claim: Textile Art Museum Australia, a public gallery in Ararat's late-Victorian Town Hall at Vincent Street and the Western Highway.
Established in 1968, its collection focuses on textile and fibre art from the early 1970s to today.
Includes Olga de Amaral's 'Coraza en dos Colores' (1973), among the most significant formative fibre works in an Australian public collection.

name: Seppelt Great Western

facts.claim: Seppelt's Great Western winery in the Grampians region dates from the 1860s and produced Australia's first traditional-method sparkling wines and sparkling reds.
Its historic underground Drives cellars are the home of the winery's cellar tours.
Cellar door at 36 Cemetery Road, Great Western.

name: Langi Ghiran State Park

facts.claim: Park 14 km east of Ararat on the Western Highway, covering 2695 ha.
A 1.8 km walking track passes Djab Wurrung rock art and a rock shelter.
The 10 km Easter Creek Track climbs through woodland and granite boulders to views over the mountains and plains.

access_note: Parks Victoria page flags "additional visitor advice"/closure banners; check before visiting. No entry fee listed.
